one_liner: C number-theory library on top of GMP; FLINT 3 (with Arb) computes pi about 2x faster than GMP and does integer matmul far faster.
what_it_does: FLINT is a C library for scalar, polynomial and matrix arithmetic, factorization and linear algebra over integers, rationals, reals (Arb balls), finite fields, number fields and p-adics. Its integer type fmpz_t stores values up to 2^62-1 inline and switches to a GMP mpz_t pointer above that, so it is a different API from mpz_t, with fmpz_set_mpz/fmpz_get_mpz for interop. FLINT 3 (2023) absorbed Arb, Antic, Calcium and Generic-Rings.
how_it_is_fast: Large integer and polynomial multiplication goes through fft_small, a truncated number-theoretic transform over several word-size primes in double precision with Chinese remaindering (van der Hoeven's approach), vectorised for AVX2 or NEON and multithreaded. Matrix multiplication (fmpz_mat_mul) uses multimodular reduction with BLAS-backed modular products instead of naive mpz loops. arb_const_pi uses binary splitting with FLINT's multiplication. The inline small-integer fmpz form avoids heap allocation for word-size entries.
when_to_use: Integer matrices and polynomials with small to medium entries, where fmpz_mat_mul is roughly 180x (10-bit) to 3.5x (1000-bit) faster than naive GMP loops
Huge single multiplications or constants (pi, e, special functions) at millions of digits, especially with flint_set_num_threads
Computer algebra and number theory: factorization, finite fields, number fields, rigorous ball arithmetic (Arb)
x86-64 with AVX2 or ARM64 with NEON, where fft_small is enabled
when_not_to_use: Element-by-element mpz-style code: FLINT's own naive fmpz matmul is no faster than GMP at 100/1000 bits (0.0213 vs 0.0172 s, 0.163 vs 0.159 s)
When you need a drop-in mpz_t/mpz_class replacement; the API is fmpz_t and you must rewrite calls
Projects that cannot accept LGPL-3.0-or-later (dynamic linking or relinkable objects required)
Platforms without AVX2/NEON, where fft_small is unavailable and large multiplies fall back to slower paths
Header-only or no-dependency setups: it needs GMP 6.2.1+ and MPFR 4.1.0+ plus an autotools build

integration.dependencies: GMP >= 6.2.1, MPFR >= 4.1.0; optional BLAS for matrix multiplication
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler (GCC/Clang); autotools on Unix, CMake on Windows
integration.platforms: Linux/Unix, macOS, Windows (CMake, MinGW64); fft_small needs x86-64 AVX2 (--enable-avx2) or aarch64 NEON
integration.thread_safety: Thread-safe by default (thread-local caches via --enable-tls); internal parallelism is opt-in with flint_set_num_threads (default 1); call flint_cleanup_master before exit to free all caches
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it uses GMP underneath and converts to and from mpz_t, but the speedups come only through FLINT's fmpz/arb/mat APIs

gotchas: Build with optimisation: issue #2852 reported fft_small 10x slower than GMP on Zen 5, but the cause was CFLAGS=-g0 overriding configure's -O flags; with -O3 it was about 3x faster than GMP
AVX2 is not on by default; pass --enable-avx2 on x86-64 to get fft_small
fmpz_t is an array-of-one type; index arrays with pointer arithmetic, and pair fmpz_init with fmpz_clear (memory from flint_malloc must be freed with flint_free)
Multithreading is off until you call flint_set_num_threads(n); the 8-thread pi and matmul figures need it
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick FLINT over mp++ or ctbignum when operands are large or the work is matrix, polynomial or constant computation; those two win on fixed small limb counts and per-operation overhead. Pick it over DoT or the AVX-512 Montgomery code when you need a maintained, licensed library instead of research kernels.
verified_claims_summary: On an 8-core Ryzen 7 PRO 5850U (Zen 3), FLINT's arb_const_pi computed 100 million digits of pi in 31.6 s versus 62.1 s for GMP-chudnovsky (about 2x), and in 9.34 s on 8 threads (about 6.6x). A 100x100 fmpz_mat_mul took 0.0000678/0.00235/0.0456 s at 10/100/1000-bit entries versus 0.0122/0.0172/0.159 s for naive GMP mpz loops. The numbers are first-party and no compiler or flags are given.
